newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES BEAT FLYERS.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-SABRES BEAT FLYERS.

text.p: Mike Peca's power-play goal 42 seconds into overtime lifted the Buffalo Sabres to a 3-2 victory over the Philadelphia Flyers in a matchup of division leaders in the Eastern Conference on Tuesday.

Philadelphia had a chance to grab the lead but Dominik Hasek stoned John LeClair on a breakaway with 50 seconds left in regulation. Shortly afterward, Mikael Renberg was called for interference, giving Buffalo the power play.

At Florida, Robert Svehla scored one goal and set up another, and Mike Hough added a key insurance goal late in the second period as the Florida Panthers snapped a four-game losing streak with a 3-2 victory over the New York Islanders.
Ray Sheppard had a power-play goal and Bill Lindsay had two assists for Florida, which won for just the second time in 12 games (2-8-2).
"It was a good win that we needed desperately," Florida coach Doug MacLean said. "I thought our penalty killing was outstanding."
At New Jersey, Bobby Holik scored twice as the red-hot New Jersey Devils tied a season-high with five first-period goals and cruised to their seventh win in eight games, 6-1 over the Edmonton Oilers.
